messages:
alex: noticing a sharp p99 spike for hosted API around 10:02 UTC, looks correlated with a single tenant. p99 jumped ~180ms -> ~1.2s. p95 up as well. alerting here so we can triage quickly
infra-bot: alert: hosted-api.p99 > 800ms (10:02:14 UTC). group: eng-runtime. runbook: perf-triage -> #eng-runtime.
maya: can you post the tenant id and recent queue depth + rate limiter metrics? also any recent deploys?
alex: tenant=tenant-42. no deploys in past hour. queue_depth metric spiked to ~300 concurrent queued requests at ~10:01:50, sustained ~45s. backend throughput dropped ~30%.
chris: grabbing kernel selector logs and kvcache stats now. initial glance: lots of small requests (~8-16 tokens) causing KV priming churn + batch sampler creating many tiny batches. sampler fallback threshold triggered which forced aux kernel on some hosts.
chris: paste logs snippet:
```
[10:01:47] kernel-selector: sequence_len=12, sampler_bucket=small, prefer_primary=false, fallback_aux=true
[10:01:48] kvcache: priming_miss_rate=0.72, eviction_rate=0.09, active_keys=1.2M
[10:01:49] batcher: avg_batch_size=2.1, batching_delay_ms=12
```
maya: oof priming_miss_rate 72% is brutal. that explains per-token work + kernel fallback. anything unusual in tenant's request pattern?
alex: tenant-42 traffic pattern changed at 09:58 — burst of 20 req/s of short prompts, likely a client-side fan-out. their per-tenant concurrency was high; rate limiter configured to 50rps burst but steady concurrency not constrained.
tina: I'm looking at per-tenant rate limits: config shows `tenant_limits.tenant-42.concurrent=200` and `burst=50`. we should throttle to protect shared pools. propose temp change to concurrent=40.
chris: kernel fallback explanation: primary kernel stays optimal for steady medium batches; with tiny batches and high KV miss, the runtime switches to aux kernel path (more memory-heavy, slower) to avoid OOMs under priming. combined with small batch overhead -> p99 spike.
samira: can we confirm host-level memory pressure? any OOM/kernels swapped logs?
chris: host mem usage climbed ~65% -> 88% on a subset of nodes serving tenant-42. no OOMs but ksm/allocator started reclaiming, which increased latency. kernel selector log shows `prefer_primary=false` decisions based on free_mem_pct < 22.
maya: TL;DR: short-request storm + KV priming churn -> cache eviction -> kernel fallback -> small batches -> latency tail. mitigation options?
alex: immediate mitigations I can push: 1) per-tenant concurrency cap down to 40 (tina), 2) kernel override on affected pool to force primary kernel (chris), 3) increase kvcache window on affected hosts (risky), 4) route tenant to dedicated pool if available.
tina: I'll change the tenant config to concurrent=40 and reduce burst to 20 now. applying in 2m.
chris: I can flip `force_primary_kernel=true` for pool `hosted-gpu-2` for a quick test. will do a canary on 2 hosts first. note: if memory pressure persists, forcing primary may increase OOM risk but should reduce latency vs aux.
samira: I'll open an incident ticket and add notes + dashboards (INC-2026). recording play-by-play and assigning owners.
alex: post-change metrics: after tina's throttle (10:06) queue_depth dropped from 300 -> 40 over ~20s, p99 fell to ~260ms, p95 -> 320ms. good immediate improvement.
chris: canary kernel override on 2 hosts applied at 10:08. on canary p99 ~220ms. pushing to remaining hosts in pool in 2m if stable.
maya: long-term: need sampler/batcher changes to avoid creating tiny batches for short prompt workloads and smarter KV priming (e.g., prefix caching or batching priming). also consider auto-per-tenant backpressure when priming_miss_rate > threshold.
alex: agreed. action items:
- samira: create incident ticket (INC-2026) and document timeline (assigned)
- tina: tenant throttle change (done)
- chris: kernel override rollout to pool and post rollback plan (in progress)
- maya: spearhead batching/sampler PR to increase min batch window for small token workloads (next week)
- alex: watch metrics and confirm no regressions (monitoring)

samira: INC-2026 created: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026. adding owners + links to dashboards.
chris: rolling override to remaining pool hosts at 10:11. will pause if memory errors appear.
tina: tenant throttle applied and propagated. seeing drop in request fan-out. good.
alex: follow-up: we should add a kvcache health alert (priming_miss_rate > 0.5 for 30s) to catch this earlier. putting it on my board.
maya: also add a perf test for tiny-prompt burst pattern to our CI perf bucket (simulate tenant-42).
samira: logging actions in INC-2026 and will schedule a 30-min postmortem for 10:40.
alex: thanks everyone. initial mitigation worked; leaving open until we have a longer-term fix. :thumbsup:
chris: thumbs. will prepare kernel-override rollback steps in case of memory regressions.
maya: adding sampler PR draft link to incident ticket.
samira: postmortem scheduled. closing active alert but keeping channel pinned to incident.
